meta.note: Reference 84 does not appear in torahData.js — zero cause/effect (eitza/cause) edges exist in the dataset for this Torah. All nodes were already identified and assigned to packages via the bechina analysis and gap analysis (torah_84_packages.json and torah_84_additions.json). The Torah source text does contain implicit eitza relationships (described below in source_text_eitza_observations) but these have not yet been added to torahData.js as edges.

source_text_eitza_observations.note: The following cause/effect relationships are present in the Torah source text but do not yet exist as edges in torahData.js. They are documented here for future dataset enrichment.

potential_eitza_edges.proof: בַּמֶּה הֶאֱרַכְתָּ יָמִים... וַתְּרָן הָיִיתִי בְּמָמוֹנִי — the Tanna asks 'through what did you lengthen your days' (= enter the hidden good), and the answer is: generosity with money. Package 1 is the gate/path; Package 3 is the destination.

מִסִּטְרָא דִּימִינָא מֹחָא חִוָּרָא כְּכַסְפָּא... נַעֲשִׂין חִוָּרָא כְּכַסְפָּא — from the right side, the brain becomes white like silver, and the accusers become defenders. The right-side quality (Package 1) causes the transformation/neutralization of the evil forces (Package 2).
potential_eitza_edges.note: This is the Torah's central eitza argument: the right-side quality neutralizes the blocking forces, transforming accuser into defender.

potential_eitza_edges.proof: אִנּוּן נְטִירִין וּנְחָשִׁים וְעַקְרַבִּים מְבַלְבְּלִין מַחֲשַׁבְתֵּהּ, דְּלָא יֵעוֹל — the foreign thoughts confuse one's mind so that one cannot ENTER the hidden good. Package 2 blocks access to Package 3.
potential_eitza_edges.note: Negative causation: foreign thoughts PREVENT access to the hidden good. This is the evil-side eitza flow.
